I'm in the field of education and I constantly hear teachers, students, and parents complain that there is "too much testing." But then I watch in public and private schools students are pushed through who have not mastered the material, have their grades padded because the parents complain, or are just given super easy material so that a schools numbers look good. You end up in a situation where a student who has straight A's bombs their SATs because they haven't encountered anything that difficult before. Nationwide standardized tests are the only way to assess student ability in a somewhat objective manner. We need more and they need to be harder and we need to be willing to fail more students. Otherwise, the US is going to continue to fall behind other countries in the developed world in terms of academic performance.

Rant ended.
The US needs more rigorous standardized testing, not less.

Standardized testing is not the solution. Education needs a complete and thorough overhaul in the US. The crux of the education problems in America is in deciding what belongs in the baseline education and what should be taught in specialized educational tracks. The idea that we should teach everyone the same then let them sort it all out after leaving school is laughable. A solid core education consisting of language skills, mathematics, history and science should be taught through the 8th grade. High school should be where we start differentiating students by their aptitudes and interests. Standardized testing can be used to asses the primary education core years, but the goal of it should be to measure and gauge aptitude not try to force conformity across the student body. Not every person is capable of the thinking and ability needed for all subject matter. We see this is the case even in college graduates who can quote verbatim material they were programmed with but cannot form a unique and independent critical thought on their own. This is a symptom of a serious flaw in the education system.

Aptitude issues need to be identified earlier and students need to be given opportunities in areas where they can actually excel rather than be hindered. Modern education in the US holds the goal of producing an endless stream of college bound automatons who will take thousands of dollars in loans to attend high tuition schools and end up in dead job markets. The current system is broken, but it is not the total fault of the students, frontline teachers and parents. The system used to work better until education became a profit-first industry. Not everyone needs a college degree or should have one. We need to get back to a world of learning by doing and not be example. School does little to teach people how to live and work. Those skills can only be learned by experience so why pretend that education is the only answer? Why pretend that there is some magic standardized test that can fix everything? I hear what you are saying with your rant, but the part we need to make harder is not the standardized tests but the ability of a handful of people in education to dictate the rules of learning. We need to fix the problems in education through resetting and simplifying things not adding more layers on top.
